pr_title: Fixes issue where a deleted AAP Job causes terraform plan to fail
pr_body:
Updates the behavior for the `aap_job` resource to handle a 404 error in the `Read` method. A 404 error indicates the job recorded in terraform state was created by the provider but has since been deleted from AAP. As noted in #59, this scenario is common because AAP cleans up old jobs by default and results in plan failures that require manual state modification.

With this change, we remove the resource from the state if a 404 is encountered, so that the plan marks it as disappeared and plans to re-create. On apply, it is re-created. I've verified the acceptance tests locally against AAP 2.5.

This PR also updates the regex patterns in the acceptance tests to support AAP 2.5 and configured `main.go` to support debugging with a `-debug` flag.

Fixes #59

pr_title: 4.x: Allow BatchStatements to be LWT
pr_body:
Previously all DefaultBatchStatements would always return `false` when `isLWT()` was called. This would cause the driver to route the batch based on the first non null routing information found in a batch but using regular rules rather than rules for LWT queries, even if a LWT query was inside the batch.

Now LWT routing will be used for DefaultBatchStatements if somewhere along the way an LWT query was added to the batch. This can also be controlled explicitly regardless of batch contents with
`BatchStatementBuilder#setIsLWT(boolean)`.

Fixes: https://github.com/scylladb/java-driver/issues/488

3. When you call `IsLWT()` if `isLWT` is `null` you resolves it via `resolveIsLWT`

It will help you with all the cases when you set `setIsLWT` and then manipulate with the batch.

+In this approach you use a primary node and one or more worker nodes. Within the primary node you initialize a W&B run. For each worker node, initialize a run using the run ID used by the primary node. During training each worker node logs to the same run ID as the primary node. W&B aggregates metrics from all nodes and displays them in the W&B App UI.

+Within the primary node, initialize a W&B run with [`wandb.init`]({{< relref "/ref/python/init.md" >}}). Pass in a `wandb.Settings` object to the `settings` parameter (`wandb.init(settings=wandb.Settings()`) wit with the following:

pr_title: Make Storage objects picklable and resumable by mp.Pool workers
pr_body:
# Pull Request

## Title

Make Storage objects picklable and resumable by mp.Pool workers.

______________________________________________________________________

## Description

To support a `ParallelTrialScheduler` with `Trials` running thru `TrialRunners` in separate processes using `multiprocessing.Pool` we need to be able to "send" all necessary state to "blank" python processes using pickle since python doesn't actually use a `fork` strategy for multiprocessing.

This change enables that by doing the following:

1. Allow pickling the core `Storage` class by hooking `__getstate__` and `__setstate__` to disconnect the `Engine` prior to pickling and reconnect on unpickling (restore).
2. Allow recreating an `Experiment` and `Trial` object by fetching it from the `Storage` by `experiment_id` and `trial_id` respectively.

These two things allow gathering the details necessary for a `TrialRunner` running in a separate child process to reconnect to the DB independently, `run_trial`, and save the telemetry and results to the DB.
After which, the "MainProcess" can `load` the results from the Experiment from the Storage again to `bulk_register` the scores from those completed `Trials` and start a new set.

______________________________________________________________________

## Type of Change

- 🛠️ Bug fix
- ✨ New feature
- 🔄 Refactor
- 🧪 Tests

______________________________________________________________________

## Testing

- [x] New CI tests

______________________________________________________________________

## Additional Notes (optional)

This change should have no impact on the existing `SyncScheduler`.

pr_title: feat(outputs.health): Add max time between metrics check
pr_body:
## Summary
This adds a new check to the `health` output plugin that can detect moments when no metrics are flowing through `telegraf`. For example, when impacted by issues like https://github.com/influxdata/telegraf/issues/16070

This is disabled by default, and can be enabled using the new configuration options:

```
[[outputs.health]]
  service_address = "http://:8080"
  max_time_between_metrics = "1s"
  unhealthy_if_metrics_are_delayed = true
```

Besides the included unittests, this change was validated running `telegraf` with the following configuration:

```
[[inputs.internal]]
  interval = "20s"

[[outputs.health]]
  service_address = "http://:8080"
  max_time_between_metrics = "1s"
  unhealthy_if_metrics_are_delayed = true
```

And querying the health status using: 
```
while true; do curl -X GET localhost:8080; sleep 0.01; done
```

1. Telegraf starts healthy.
2. Once 1s passes after the first internal metrics are written, the status changes to unhealthy
3. After that, every 20s, it reports OK for 1s and then goes back to unhealthy.

This PR replaces the previous implementation attempt done in https://github.com/influxdata/telegraf/pull/16212
For more context, refer to [this slack thread](https://influxcommunity.slack.com/archives/CH99HUH8V/p1736782025589019?thread_ts=1731947234.950749&cid=CH99HUH8V)

pr_title: fix(RHINENG-13683): Correctly process multiple messages for the same host in the same MQ batch
pr_body:
# Overview

This PR is being created to address [RHINENG-13683](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHINENG-13683) and [RHINENG-17921](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHINENG-17921).

Summary of the issue: When we are processing a payload message, we check if the host already exists in the DB, if yes we update it, if no we create a new host. However, we only flush and commit our changes after a batch of MQ messages have been processed. So, if we are processing 2nd input message for the same host within the same MQ batch, we don't find the existing host (because it is not committed yet) and we create a new one - and we end up with a duplicate.

This PR creates new methods for finding existing hosts by canonical facts in a provided list of hosts. These methods (`multiple_canonical_facts_host_query_in_memory`, `contains_no_incorrect_facts_filter_in_memory`, and `matches_at_least_one_canonical_fact_filter_in_memory`) are creating a python filter queries (NOT sqlalchemy query) which do the same thing as the existing DB query methods, but these filters are intended to be used on an existing in-memory list of hosts, instead of for querying the DB.

Functions like `find_existing_host` are now accepting one additional parameter (`from_hosts`). If this parameter is provided, then they use the new python filter to filter out the provided list of hosts. Otherwise, they use the old DB queries.

In the event loop, we pass the `processed_rows` to the lower-level methods `handle_message` and `process_message`, which use this list to first check if we can find a match inside the `processed_rows`. Only if we can't, then we try to query the DB.

My main concern is around metrics. The `find_existing_host` and other functions are collecting metrics for the dedup process, which will happen only in-memory in this case, so the metrics will be affected by this. Do you think this is an issue?

## PR Checklist

- [ ] Keep PR title short, ideally under 72 characters
- [ ] Descriptive comments provided in complex code blocks
- [ ] Include raw query examples in the PR description, if adding/modifying SQL query
- [ ] Tests: validate optimal/expected output

- [ ] Uses [type hinting](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html), if convenient
- [ ] Documentation, if this PR changes the way other services interact with host inventory
- [ ] Links to related PRs

## Secure Coding Practices Documentation Reference

You can find documentation on this checklist [here](https://github.com/RedHatInsights/secure-coding-checklist).

## Secure Coding Checklist

- [ ] Input Validation
- [ ] Output Encoding
- [ ] Authentication and Password Management
- [ ] Session Management
- [ ] Access Control
- [ ] Cryptographic Practices
- [ ] Error Handling and Logging
- [ ] Data Protection
- [ ] Communication Security
- [ ] System Configuration
- [ ] Database Security
- [ ] File Management
- [ ] Memory Management
- [ ] General Coding Practices

## Summary by Sourcery

Refactor host deduplication and message processing to enable correct handling of multiple messages for the same host within a single MQ batch by passing already-processed hosts in memory to lookup and add operations.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure subsequent messages for the same host in the same MQ batch match the already-processed host instead of creating duplicates.

Enhancements:
- Extend find_existing_host and related lookup methods to accept an optional in-memory host list and branch between DB and in-memory queries.
- Propagate the processed_rows list through handle_message and process_message in MQ consumers and update add_host signature with an existing_host parameter.
- Introduce in-memory filtering functions (multiple_canonical_facts_host_query_in_memory, contains_no_incorrect_facts_filter_in_memory, matches_at_least_one_canonical_fact_filter_in_memory).
- Add type annotations to various functions (parse_operation_message, common_message_parser, update_query_for_owner_id, create_mock_identity_with_org_id, get_staleness_obj, initialize_thread_local_storage, operation_results_to_event_type).
- Add validation in write_add_update_event_message to enforce non-null event_type and platform_metadata.
- Remove unused single_canonical_fact_host_query function.

Tests:
- Update tests to account for the new processed_rows argument in handle_message and process_message signatures.

## Summary by Sourcery

Implement in-memory deduplication of hosts within an MQ batch by extending host lookup functions to accept a list of already-processed hosts and propagating processed rows through message consumers to prevent duplicate host creation.

Bug Fixes:
- Deduplicate multiple messages for the same host in a single MQ batch by matching against already-processed hosts before querying the database

Enhancements:
- Extend find_existing_host and related lookup methods to accept an optional in-memory host list and branch between DB and in-memory queries
- Introduce Python-based in-memory filter helpers for canonical facts matching to mirror existing DB queries
- Propagate processed_rows through HBI message consumers and update event loop and post_process_rows to commit and publish batched events using in-memory deduplication

Tests:
- Add tests for in-batch deduplication, two-host batch processing, and fallback to DB-based deduplication

Chores:
- Add type annotations across multiple functions, validate non-null event payloads, and remove unused single_canonical_fact_host_query function

+---
+layout: post
+title: "Debezium as part of your AI solution"
+date: 2025-05-19
+tags: [ demo, ai, rag ]
+author: jpechane
+---
+
+One question that we encountered recently is how to effectively integrate change data capture (CDC) with AI workloads — particularly for scenarios in which critical organizational knowledge is not publicly available.
+To help you to take advantage of your internal data, Debezium 3.1 introduces AI-focused features such as the Embeddings SMT and the Milvus sink, which you can combine to supply inputs to an LLM.  
+You can read more about these enhancements in the https://debezium.io/blog/2025/04/02/debezium-3-1-final-released/[Debezium 3.1 release notes].
+
++++<!-- more -->+++
+
+:imagesdir: /assets/images/2025-05-22-debezium-as-part-of-your-ai-solution
+
+== Introduction
+
+In this post, we'll show how Debezium, Milvus, and Ollama can work together to form a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline.
+By capturing changes from a relational database, enriching them with vector embeddings, and enabling similarity search across these vectors, you can build AI-driven applications that are powered by up-to-date, domain-specific knowledge.
+
+Let's look at an example that illustrates how you can use Debezium to enrich your AI applications with knowledge captured from experts within your organization.
+
+Suppose that our organization introduces a new AI-driven application that is backed by an LLM.
+To enrich and extend the language model, we want to take advantage of internal organizational knowledge that is stored in text documents in a PostgreSQL database.
+Whenever users within the organization interact with the AI application, we want to make sure that its responses are informed by the most current local knowledge.
+Because the local knowledge that is stored in the PostgreSQL database is in constant flux, with documents being added, updated, or withdrawn to comply with regulatory requirements, we need a solution that has the agility to keep up with these changes. 
+
+The common solution to address this problem is to implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
+This post demonstrates how to use Debezium to build a CDC-fed RAG system that uses the following components:
+
+* A PostgreSQL database for data storage
+* Milvus vector database
+* Debezium Server to feed Milvus from PostgreSQL
+* A local https://ollama.com/[Ollama] hosted LLM
+* A Java application that interacts with the LLM and uses RAG to provide prompt context
+
+== What is RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)?
+
+Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an AI technique that combines information retrieval with generative models to produce more accurate and contextually relevant responses.
+Instead of relying solely on a model's internal knowledge, RAG pipelines retrieve relevant documents or data from an external source (like a vector database) and use that information to enrich the model's responses.
+In our scenario, Debezium, Milvus, and Ollama work together to form a RAG workflow: data changes are captured and vectorized, stored in Milvus, and then retrieved to augment LLM outputs with up-to-date, domain-specific information.
+
+== What is Debezium Server?
+
+https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/3.1/operations/debezium-server.html[Debezium Server] is a Debezium implementation that you can use to stream change events from databases to various sinks without the need to deploy a Kafka cluster.
+It provides a lightweight way to consume CDC events and forward them to destinations from which they can be consumed by other applications.
+Debezium Server also supports the use of Kafka Connect single message transformations within its processing pipeline.
+
+== What is Milvus?
+
+Milvus is a specialized vector database designed for similarity search and AI-heavy workloads.
+Whether it's product recommendations, image search, or any other use case that relies on fast vector retrieval, Milvus is built for that.
+A vector database and fast vector retrieval is the heart of any RAG solution.
+The vector database stores so called *embeddings* - vector representations of the data that can be used for tasks like similarity search or clustering.
+Based on similarities between a prompt and the stored data, the AI application extends the context of the prompt.
+
+=== Why Milvus as a Sink?
+
+For applications where you need up-to-date vector representations of your data, pushing changes from a transactional database into Milvus makes a lot of sense.
+By using Milvus, not only can you keep your AI models in sync with operational data, you can also offload similarity search to a system that is built for it.
+
+=== How Debezium Milvus Sink Works
+
+A typical deployment of Milvus sink uses the following workflow:
+
+* The Debezium connector captures changes from a source database.
+* If the source database does not contain a field with embeddings, then the https://debezium.io/blog/2025/04/02/debezium-3-1-final-released/#new-features-and-improvements-ai[FieldToEmbedding SMT] is used to enrich change events with vector embeddings.
+* Milvus sink writes the vector data into Milvus.
+* Milvus stores and indexes the vectors for fast similarity search.
+
+== Example application
+
+This blogpost is based on the https://github.com/debezium/debezium-examples/tree/main/ai-rag[Debezium ai-rag] example application.
+Let's go step-by-step through the details and internals of the application so you can easily build your own.
+
+image::overview.png[image,caption="Figure 1: Architecture",width=800,role=centered-image]
+
+The application architecture consists of the following two flows, which share a common Milvus instance:
+
+* Data pipeline
+* AI application
+
+The data pipeline ingests data into Milvus, while the AI application queries Milvus to find similarities in the data.
+
+=== Data pipeline
+
+Our organization sources documents in an https://arxiv.org/[arXiv service] that provides scholarly articles for download in different formats.
+The test application downloads a requested article based on its identifier and stores it in a PostgreSQL table.
+
+The PostgreSQL table is created with the following https://github.com/debezium/debezium-examples/blob/main/ai-rag/config-postgres/ai-sample-data.sql[DDL]:
+[source,sql]
+----
+CREATE TABLE documents (
+  id VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
+  metadata JSON,
+  text TEXT
+);
+ALTER TABLE documents REPLICA IDENTITY FULL;
+----
+
+The replica identity of the table is set to `FULL`, so Debezium preserves the original state of a row in update and delete messages.
+Our demo doesn't require preservation of the original row state, but being able to refer back to the original state is useful for some implementations.
+
+Upon user request, the application downloads documents in text form and stores them in the table.
+Debezium stores the document identifier in the `id` field of the event; the textual representation of the article in the `text` field; and JSON metadata `{"id:" "<document id>"}` in metadata.
+The table does not provide a column with embeddings, so Debezium must use its `FieldToEmbedding` SMT (described later) to calculate them.
+
+In our environment, we run a local LLM that is based on the Ollama LLM framework.
+For the model, we selected https://ollama.com/library/granite3.1-dense:2b[granite3.1-dense:2b], a text-only model that optimized for RAG.
+Our model is one of large family of open-source https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite[IBM Granite models], but the application is not limited to it and can use an arbitrary model.
+
+Debezium Server provides an interface between the PostgreSQL store and the Milvus sink.
+Because embeddings are not provided, we can use the https://github.com/debezium/debezium-examples/blob/main/ai-rag/config-server/application.properties#L16[Debezium FieldToEmbedding SMT] to calculate them and store them a field named `vector`.
+
+Our application uses LangChain4j Milvus store module internally so we will keep the default collection structure https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j/blob/main/langchain4j-milvus/src/main/java/dev/langchain4j/store/embedding/milvus/MilvusEmbeddingStore.java[expected by it]
+
+* `id` - `VarChar`
+* `metadata` - `JSON`
+* `text` -`VarChar`
+* `vector` - `FloatVector`
+
+There is a known https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j/issues/2834[issue] in the module that causes an application failure when the store is empty.
+We are going to store one dummy document in the database (and thus in Milvus) to work around it.
+
+== AI Application
+
+The AI application is the application that interacts with LLM and extends the prompt with data loaded from Milvus stored base on the data and prompt embeddings similarity.

pr_title: add: Parse `Scenario` as a synonym for `Scenario Outline`
pr_body:
In cucumber/gherkin, the `Scenario:` and `Scenario Outline:` keywords are interchangeable. Either may have (or not have) an `Examples:` table.

We still need to differentiate between `OutlineNode` and `ScenarioNode` in the parsed result, for BC and because Behat treats these differently at runtime.

However, we can safely parse a `Scenario:` that contains an `Examples:` table (which would have previously been invalid) to an `OutlineNode` - exactly as if the user had written `Scenario Outline:`.

This does require refactoring how we parse tags, because:

* Previously, we could make assumptions based on whether we were expecting (or had already seen) an Examples table.
* Now, we can't tell from the tags alone whether they belong to an Examples table, or mark the end of the current Scenario and the start of the next.

Therefore, we now scan ahead to predict which node the tags are attached to. This also allows us to throw a clearer exception if tags are found in unexpected places in the document.

Relates to #153

For both CUDA and HIP, two overloads of Kokkos::Experimental::inclusive_scan have been implemented which call the corresponding thrust::inclusive_scan functions, under device execution space.

Rough performance numbers (based on just a single run of the scan operation) can be observed by using the following two test codes:

Thrust: [thrust_single_test_cpp.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18504552/thrust_single_test_cpp.txt)

Total number of elements in the input = 1e8. The input contains values 0, 1, 2, ..., 1e8 - 1. Scans based on sum and max binary operations were tested.

thrust::inclusive_scan 
sum (default): 2467 us, sum (functor): 5460 us, max (functor): 6165 us

With modified Kokkos (calling thrust::inclusive_scan)

With original Kokkos (calling Kokkos::parallel_scan)
sum (default): 11488 us, sum (functor): 9618 us, max (functor): 9743 us

As a point of reference, Kokkos::parallel_scan with a summation based functor takes 12998 us based on the following code:

## What is this fixing or adding?
This uses `classvar_matrix` introduced with https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/pull/4648 to split some subtests generating worlds into their own class, so they can be parallelized with `pytest -n`. Most of those tests are only running with a specific configuration, are not run by GitHub actions. 

For the normal tests executed by GitHub actions, they now run in 20 seconds instead of 30 seconds.  
For the long tests only executed locally, this cut the time need to run the long tests from 18 minutes to 5 minutes.

review_comment:
I can answer as to why this exists, as I believe it was originally my addition. I won't fight on it being good or not though, because I agree it's a weird pattern.

My reasoning for that was: I want this test to always run, as it is pretty darn good at catching "big" errors that pass generation but lead to illegal states. But these errors are setting dependent, and unlike the test for option pairs, this one has the potential to catch any combination of settings, not just the ones that are 2-values-away-from-default. As a result though, it has massively diminishing returns, so I didn't want to run it much on the main pipeline.

So the idea is: If something is **very** broken, the main pipeline can catch it, as most or all option combinations will lead to it. If something is slightly broken and requires specific settings, then the long tests have a decent chance of catching it.

+// Constants for Azure configuration options
+const (
+	AdlsSasTokenPrefix         = "adls.sas-token."
+	AdlsConnectionStringPrefix = "adls.connection-string."
+	AdlsSharedKeyAccountName   = "adls.auth.shared-key.account.name"
+	AdlsSharedKeyAccountKey    = "adls.auth.shared-key.account.key"
+	AdlsEndpoint               = "adls.endpoint"
+	AdlsProtocol               = "adls.protocol"
+
+	// Not in use yet
+	// AdlsReadBlockSize          = "adls.read.block-size-bytes"
+	// AdlsWriteBlockSize         = "adls.write.block-size-bytes"
+)
+
+// Construct a Azure bucket from a URL
+func createAzureBucket(ctx context.Context, parsed *url.URL, props map[string]string) (*blob.Bucket, error) {
+	adlsSasTokens := propertiesWithPrefix(props, AdlsSasTokenPrefix)
+	adlsConnectionStrings := propertiesWithPrefix(props, AdlsConnectionStringPrefix)
+
+	// Construct the client
+	accountName := props[AdlsSharedKeyAccountName]
+	endpoint := props[AdlsEndpoint]
+	protocol := props[AdlsProtocol]
+
+	var client *container.Client
+
+	if accountName != "" {
+		var sharedKeyCred *azblob.SharedKeyCredential
+		var err error
+
+		if accountKey, ok := props[AdlsSharedKeyAccountKey]; ok {
+			svcURL, err := azureblob.NewServiceURL(&azureblob.ServiceURLOptions{
+				AccountName:   accountName,
+				Protocol:      protocol,
+				StorageDomain: endpoint,
+			})
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, err
+			}
+			containerURL, err := url.JoinPath(string(svcURL), parsed.Host)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, err
+			}
+			sharedKeyCred, err = azblob.NewSharedKeyCredential(accountName, accountKey)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed azblob.NewSharedKeyCredential: %w", err)
+			}
+
+			client, err = container.NewClientWithSharedKeyCredential(containerURL, sharedKeyCred, nil)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed container.NewClientWithSharedKeyCredential: %w", err)
+			}
+		} else if sasToken, ok := adlsSasTokens[accountName]; ok {
+			svcURL, err := azureblob.NewServiceURL(&azureblob.ServiceURLOptions{
+				AccountName:   accountName,
+				SASToken:      sasToken,
+				Protocol:      protocol,
+				StorageDomain: endpoint,
+			})
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, err
+			}
+
+			containerURL, err := url.JoinPath(string(svcURL), parsed.Host)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, err
+			}
+
+			client, err = container.NewClientWithNoCredential(containerURL, nil)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed container.NewClientWithNoCredential: %w", err)
+			}
+		} else if connectionString, ok := adlsConnectionStrings[accountName]; ok {
+			client, err = container.NewClientFromConnectionString(connectionString, parsed.Host, nil)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed container.NewClientFromConnectionString: %w", err)
+			}
+		}
+
+		bucket, err := azureblob.OpenBucket(ctx, client, nil)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+
+		return bucket, nil

pr_title: Enable Request Level Excluded Locations to Metadata API calls

# Description

Request level excluded locations were not available for nested metadata calls. This could cause potential latency issue with high demend locations. With this changes metadata calls will also be re-routed to non-excluded locations.

### Changes
- Metadata API calls will now include request level excluded locations
- For metadata calls, all excluded locations in preferred locations will be re-ordered to the end of the available locations. This means, even thought some locations were excluded, if all non-excluded locations were not available, the excluded locations will be used during API calls

pr_title: feat(upstream): Add upstream-form component
pr_body:
## Motivation
Configuration for APISIX Upstreams is a common requirement across various parts of the apisix-unofficial-dashboard, such as Routes and potentially Services in the future. To promote code reuse, maintain consistency, and simplify maintenance, this PR introduces a dedicated, reusable component (UpstreamForm) for handling upstream configurations.

## Changes

1.  **New Component (`UpstreamForm`):**
    *   Created `src/components/upstream/upstream-form.vue` which encapsulates the UI and logic for configuring APISIX upstream objects.
    *   Supports configuration of:
        *   Load Balancer Algorithm (`type`)
        *   Upstream Type selection (Static Nodes vs. Service Discovery)
        *   Node configuration (Host, Port, Weight) with dynamic add/remove functionality.
        *   Basic Service Discovery configuration (`discovery_type`, `service_name`, `pass_host`, `upstream_host`).
        *   Retry settings (`retries`, `retry_timeout`).
        *   Protocol (`scheme`).
        *   Timeout settings (`timeout.connect`, `timeout.send`, `timeout.read`).
        *   Connection Pool (`keepalive_pool`).
        *   Basic Active Health Check configuration (enable toggle, type, core parameters, healthy/unhealthy checks).
    *   Uses `tdesign-vue-next` components and includes basic validation.
    *   Accepts upstream data via `v-model` (`modelValue` prop).
    *   Exposes `validate()` and `getApiFormattedData()` methods for form interaction and retrieving data in the expected APISIX format.
    *   Exposes a `resetForm()` method.

2.  **Supporting Files:**
    *   `src/components/upstream/constants.ts`: Defines constants for select options (Load Balancer, Discovery Type, Protocol, Health Check Types) and validation rules.
    *   `src/components/upstream/upstream-form.less`: Contains styling specific to the form component.

3.  **Test Harness:**
    *   Added `src/components/upstream/upstream-form-harness.vue` as a development/testing page for the `UpstreamForm` component.
    *   This page can be accessed via the route `/#/dev/upstream-form-harness` (ensure routing is set up if needed).

## Limitations & Future Work

This PR establishes the foundational `UpstreamForm` component. However, certain features are intentionally **not fully implemented** in this initial version:

*   **Service Discovery:** While the basic fields are present, the full logic and potential variations might require further refinement.
*   **Health Checks:** Only active health checks are partially implemented. Passive health checks and more advanced options for active checks (e.g., specific headers, full status code handling nuances) are not yet included.

The plan is to merge this component first to establish the structure. The remaining features for Service Discovery and Health Checks will be fully implemented and tested in subsequent PRs, likely when integrating this component into the Router configuration module.

pr_title: feat: uv as default package manager
pr_body:
Closes #693

The idea is to make `uv` the default package manager in actions where it can bring much value — those where potentially a lot of packages will be installed.

So far these include:
- Actions where a project's library and/or its dependencies can be installed:
  - `_doc-build-linux`
  - `_doc-build-windows`
  - `build-wheel-house`
  - `check-licenses`
  - `check-vulnerabilities`
  - `code-style`
  - `tests-pytest`

- Actions where > two packages are installed:
  - `doc-deploy-changelog`

In actions where ≤ 2 packages are being installed, the idea is that `pip` is enough and I didn't touch those. They include:
- `_release-pypi`
- `build-library`
- `doc-changelog`
- `hk-package-clean-except`
- `hk-package-clean-untagged`


Implementing `uv` support has been done in a non-intrusive way, to accommodate those that do not want to use it. In the actions where `uv` is supported, a `use-uv` input has been added which defaults to true. Therefore, setting `use-uv=false` essentially reverts those actions to how they were before.

## IMPORTANT
> [!NOTE]  
> After discussions, `use-uv` has been set to default to true across all actions. This way, any issue can quickly surface when
> users switch to `v10` for quick fixes. Also, the `use-uv` option is now available across all actions for consistency.

pr_title: sched/wqueue: Refactor delayed and periodic workqueue.
pr_body:
## Summary

This commit refactors the delayed and the periodic workqueue, and changes the timer to be set in `work_thread`. The improvements of this change are as follows:
- Fix the memory reuse problem of the original periodic workqueue implementation.  https://github.com/apache/nuttx/pull/15937#issuecomment-2808973151
- By removing the `wdog_s` structure in the `work_s` structure, the memory overhead of each `work_s` structure is reduced by about 30 bytes.
- Set the timer for each workqueue instead of each work, which improves system performance.
- Simplified the workqueue cancel processing.

# CORE-Bench

This PR contains an implementation of the [CORE-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11363) agent benchmark. The main code is in the `src/inspect_evals/core_bench` folder across the following files:
* `agent_prompts.json`: Contains agent prompts for each difficulty level.
* `Dockerfile`: [Docker-in-Docker image](https://github.com/cruizba/ubuntu-dind) which allows the agent to spin up a new container inside the sandbox it is running in. This is necessary for the medium difficulty level.
* `compose.yaml`: Docker compose file to spin up container for LLM agent to act in. Uses the Dockerfile and runs container in a privileged state to allow running docker in docker.
* `core_bench.py`: Main implementation of the task.
* `dataset.py`: Handles downloading dataset, preprocessing data, and creating samples.
* `scorer.py`: Evaluation code to measure correctness of each sample.
* `tools.py`: Defines a new vision language model tool that the agent can use inside the sandbox.
* `utils.py`: Utility functions to help with evaluation functionality in `scorer.py`.

# Model Results

| Task              | GPT-4o-mini (Paper) | GPT-4o (Paper) | GPT-4o-mini (PR) | GPT-4o (PR) |
|-------------------|---------------------|----------------|------------------|-------------|
| CORE-Bench Easy   | 44.44%              | 60.00%         |          24.4%        |       31.1%      |
| CORE-Bench Medium | 32.59%              | 57.78%         |         Not Tested         |       Not Tested      |
| CORE-Bench Hard   | 16.30%              | 21.48%         |          Not Tested        |       Not Tested      |

# Notes
* There is a large difference between this implementation and the paper results due to the use of the `basic_agent`. The paper uses a customized version of AutoGPT which wasn't ported over in this PR mostly due to it being a heavy lift to fully implement it.
* For the medium difficulty setting where the agent should run a Docker command inside the sandbox, some samples require a GPU to fully reproduce results. Make sure you are running on a machine with a GPU in order to achieve parity with the original implementation.
* The medium and hard difficulty settings were not fully evaluated due to the GPU requirement for some capsules.
* Unit tests are included.

https://github.com/dragonflydb/dragonfly/commit/91c27f1f18cb4378ca5daacbbe616855cce437fd

review_comment:
@romange @abhijat 

Each family has 64 bits available for each command in the family. Under any scenario, we should not extend the bit per family for each cloned command as it's a scarce resource and I want to keep it empty for future additions. In other words, that `++bit_index` for cloned commands is problematic not only because it consumes what's left for the future but also is unbounded (what if somebody created 100 aliases ? Not realistic but still it will overflow the bits.

I agree with @romange that we should ignore altogether those aliases unless they are called from the admin port.
So:

* We `skip acl validation` on admin port (e.g. when IsPriveledged() is true we set `skip_acl_validation` in `ConnectionContext` ctor). This is already handled -- there is no ACL auth on admin port!

* We add a flag `is_cloned` on cid to denote that the command is a clone

* Within `IsUserAllowedToInvokeCmd()` we check if `cid->IsClone()` and we reject it (we first check if `skip_acl_validation==true` upon which we return true, see the implementation it's already hadled).

* There are 3 uses of `registry` inside acl family. Namely when we parse acl's (when user issues ACL SETUSER). We need to reject the clones. This is easy, just add an extra check `cid->isClone()` and reject the command if it's a clone during any call of any of the acl family commands. 

Unless I am missing something the above should give us the right semantics:

* reject clones/aliases unless they run on admin port

pr_title: Add robust error context analysis system
pr_body:
## Overview

This PR adds a robust and dynamic error context analysis system to the codebase. The system provides detailed contextual information about errors in code, including the error location, type, severity, and suggested fixes.

## Features

- **ErrorContextAnalyzer**: A specialized class for detecting and analyzing errors in code
- **CodeError**: A class representing an error in code with detailed context information
- **Enhanced CodeAnalyzer**: Updated to integrate error context analysis
- **New API Endpoints**: Added endpoints for analyzing errors in repositories, files, and functions
- **Example Script**: Added an example script demonstrating how to use the error context analysis functionality

## Error Types Detected

The system can detect the following types of errors:

- **Syntax Errors**: Invalid syntax in code
- **Type Errors**: Type mismatches in expressions
- **Parameter Errors**: Incorrect function parameters
- **Call Errors**: Incorrect function calls
- **Undefined Variables**: Variables used without being defined
- **Unused Imports**: Imports that are not used in the code
- **Circular Imports**: Circular dependencies between files
- **Circular Dependencies**: Circular dependencies between symbols

## Context Information

For each error, the system provides detailed context information:

- **Error Type**: The type of error (syntax, type, parameter, etc.)
- **Message**: A descriptive message explaining the error
- **Location**: The file path and line number where the error occurs
- **Severity**: The severity of the error (critical, high, medium, low, info)
- **Context Lines**: The lines of code surrounding the error
- **Suggested Fix**: A suggested fix for the error

## Implementation Details

The implementation uses various techniques to detect errors:

- **AST Analysis**: Parsing the code into an abstract syntax tree to detect syntax errors and undefined variables
- **Graph Analysis**: Building dependency graphs to detect circular imports and dependencies
- **Pattern Matching**: Using regular expressions to detect potential type errors and other issues

## Documentation

Added comprehensive documentation in the README.md file, including:

- Overview of the system
- Features and capabilities
- Error types detected
- Usage examples
- API documentation
- Implementation details

## Example Usage

```python
from codegen import Codebase
from codegen_on_oss.analysis.analysis import CodeAnalyzer

# Create a codebase from a repository
codebase = Codebase.from_repo("owner/repo")

# Create an analyzer
analyzer = CodeAnalyzer(codebase)

# Analyze errors in the codebase
errors = analyzer.analyze_errors()

# Get detailed error context for a function
function_errors = analyzer.get_function_error_context("function_name")

# Get detailed error context for a file
file_errors = analyzer.get_file_error_context("path/to/file.py")
```

pr_title: Add GlowSpell
pr_body:
Adds `.targeted.GlowSpell`, a replacement for `.targeted.ext.GlowSpell`.

Example:
```yml
glow:
    spell-class: ".targeted.GlowSpell"
    key: example:glow # Specifies a namespaced key for the glow. Glows with the same key override each other. Supports replacement. Optional.
    color: red # Specifies the glow's color. Optional.
    global: true # Specifies whether the glow is only visible to the caster, or all players. Defaults to `true`.
    duration: 200 # Specifies how long the glow should last, in ticks. Only applies when the value is greater than 0. Defaults to `0`.
    priority: 20 # Specifies the priority of the glow. The glow with the highest priority will be applied. Defaults to `0`.

glow/remove:
    spell-class: ".targeted.GlowSpell"
    key: example:glow # Specifies the namespaced key of the glow to remove.
    global: true # Specifies whether to remove a global or per-player glow.
    remove: true # When `true`, the glow specified by `key` will instead be removed.
```

`general.yml` configuration:
```yml
# General options that apply to the scoreboard teams created by `.targeted.GlowSpell`. These correspond to general scoreboard teams options that can affect client behavior. See https://minecraft.wiki/w/Scoreboard#Teams.
glow-spell-scoreboard-teams:
    see-friendly-invisibles: false
    name-tag-visibility: always
    collision-rule: always
```

- No longer requires an external dependency to function. Interfaces with the `packetevents` plugin when available for better compatibility with other plugins.
- Relies on scoreboard teams and packet manipulation. As such, this spell can conflict with other plugins that interact with scoreboards, such as those that use them to manipulate the tab list, or preventing player collisions.
- Has some support for disguises from the Lib's Disguises plugin. There are issues that can be caused when using a `GlowSpell` on a disguised entity; most of these issues will likely not be fixed.

pr_title: sync policy, MIME override, encoding support, and more
pr_body:
## Synchronous policy and fixes
- Add new non-standard option `syncPolicy: "warn" | "enabled" | "disabled"` (default is "warn") to explicitly enable/disable synchronous XHR with or without warning
	- `"warn"`: enable synchronous xhr but shows a warning when the user attempts to call `xhr.open()` with sync flag:
		> [Deprecation] Synchronous XMLHttpRequest is deprecated because of its detrimental effects to the end user's experience. For more information, see https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#sync-flag
	- `"enabled"`: enable synchronous xhr, no warnings
	- `"disabled"`: disable synchronous, calling `xhr.open()` with sync flag won't show any warning, but an exception is thrown when calling `xhr.send()` afterwards:
		> Synchronous requests are disabled for this instance.
- Fix problem with data not encoded properly when using synchronous request (#29)
- Sync responses now write data into OS temporary directory instead of cwd (since rwx permissions can be altered for cwd)
- If file system operations fail, an error message will be thrown:
	> Synchronous operation aborted: Unable to access the OS temporary directory for read/write operations.
## Encoding and MIME type support
- Add `xhr.overrideMimeType(type)` (#27)
- Add support for encodings other than utf-8 (can be read from `Content-Type` header or through user's custom encoding via `xhr.overrideMimeType()`)
## Non-standard methods
- Removed `xhr.setDisableHeaderCheck()` and instead added a non-standard `disableHeaderCheck: true | false` (default is `false`)
- Add deprecation message for `xhr.getRequestHeader()`:
	> `xhr.getRequestHeader()` is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. It’s non-standard and not part of the XHR spec.
## Others
- Prevent `XMLHttpRequest` to be called without `new` operator
- Unifies `createFileOrSyncResponse` and `createResponse` into one method `createResponse`
- Brings some methods back to private scope to prevent tampering (especially the `readyState` value)
- Add immutable flags value UNSENT, OPENED, HEADERS_RECEIVED, LOADING, and DONE to both `XMLHttpRequest` and any newly-created xhr object
- Add two more options, `textDecoder: <func>` for users to specify custom text decoder (to support more range of encodings for old Node versions) and `xmlParser: <func>` to support parsing for `xhr.responseXML`

pr_title: [FIXED] Only deliver replicated message after quorum
pr_body:
Related to https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/pull/6469, about the following code:
```go
	// Update delivered first.
	o.updateDelivered(dseq, seq, dc, ts)

	// Send message.
	o.outq.send(pmsg)
```

`o.updateDelivered` requires proposing delivered state through Raft, and even if proposing fails, we immediately sent the message to the client. This is great for performance, but really bad for properly replicating this piece of data. Before the before-mentioned PR there would be a bunch of nasty side-effects of stuck consumer, perceived data loss through missed redeliveries, etc. Because clients could get messages that a new leader wouldn't know about if proposals failed.

The core issue is that we should only send the message AFTER we had quorum on updating delivered state. Otherwise the following could happen: message gets sent to the client, `updateDelivered` proposal fails, leader changes, `AckSync` will now timeout indefinitely even with retries because the new leader doesn't know this message was even delivered.

Signed-off-by: Maurice van Veen <github@mauricevanveen.com>
review_comment: The stream sequence is used as a key, which is the same for `o.pending`. That means it can only ever become as large as max length of `o.pending`, i.e. `MaxAckPending`.

+    Average Directional Index (ADX) Trend Indicator Implementation.
+    The ADX measures the strength of a trend and is

+    - **ADX**: Indicates the trend strength

+    - **DMP (+DI)**: Positive directional movement 
+      (upward trend indicator).
+    - **DMN (-DI)**: Negative directional movement 
+      (downward trend indicator).
+    Formula:
+    1. Compute **True Range (TR)**, which reflects market volatility.
+    2. Calculate the **Directional Movement (+DM / -DM)** based on 
+      high/low price action.
+    3. Apply **Moving Averages** to smooth +DM, -DM values.
+    4. Compute **ADX** as an exponentially smoothed average 
+      of the Directional Index.
+    Usage:
+    - Helps traders determine if a trend is strong 
+      enough to justify entering a trade.
+    - Can be combined with other trend indicators 
+      (e.g., moving averages) for confirmation.
+    """
+
+    def calculate_adx(
+        self, 
+        data: PriceDataFrame, 
+        config: AdxConfigDM
+    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
+        """
+        Computes the ADX, DMP (+DI), and DMN (-DI) trend indicators.
+        Args:
+            data (PriceDataFrame): Price dataset containing 
+              high, low, and close prices.
+            config (AdxConfigDM): Configuration for ADX 
+              (length, smoothing factors, drift, offset).
+        Returns:
+            pd.DataFrame: A DataFrame containing ADX, DMP, and DMN trend values.
+        Raises:
+            ValueError: If the ADX calculation returns missing 
+              values for any required component.
+        """
+        # Compute ADX and its components using pandas-ta
+        adx_ind = ta.adx(
+            high=data.high_prices,
+            low=data.low_prices,
+            close=data.close_prices,
+            length=config.length,
+            # Signal length for ADX smoothing
+            lensig=config.lensig,
+            # Scaling factor for values
+            scalar=config.scalar,  
+            # Moving average mode (e.g., EMA, SMA)
+            mamode=config.mamode,  
+            drift=config.drift,
+            offset=config.offset
+        )
+        #  Validate if all required components exist

+            for indicator in ["ADX", "DMP", "DMN"]

Fixes:
-  `_select_parser` could be invoked with a `Path`, while it expects a `FileSystemEntry`. - Systemd network parser did not collapse singleton values
- When multiple sections with the same name are encountered, the resulting key is a list of those sections:
Example:
```
key value1
   key2 value2a
key value1
   key2 value2b
   key3 value3b
```
  
 now parses as  `{"key value1": [{"key2": "value2a"}, {"key2": "value2b", "key3": "value3b"}]}`. Previously, this parsed as `{"key value1": {"key2": ["value2a", "value2b"], "key3": "value3b"}}`, where the parallel lists could become misaligned.

Supports:
- Drop files when invoking parse with a systemd file
- Empty value now clears corresponding key when merging systemd files.

Updated the `ExportPartnersCSVService` to export all of the `Partner::Profile` fields, filtered based on which `Partner.partials_to_show` the partner org selected.

The partials which are always shown (`agency_information` and `partner_settings`) will always have their fields included in the export.

Areas served was already implemented as described.

The database seed was updated to create partner profiles with dummy data in all of the fields if those partners are established (ready for approval, approved or require_recertification). The seed also only adds fields for optional partials which the partner's org has enabled.

To handle cases where `ExportPartnersCSVService` was called with no partners, `Organization` was updated to have a function that checks `partials_to_show` and `Partner`'s version of the function was udpated to refer to the `Organization` one. The same was done for the `ALL_PARTIALS` constant as `Organziation` already had a definition for it.

The existing `ExportPartnersCSVService` included some fields which were from optional partials (for example `primary_contact_name` from the `executive_director` partial). Similarly, some of the profile fields the database seed were already populating were from optional partials. These were not changed to be contingent on those partials being enabled for the sake of not changing the existing behavior and "hiding" data someone might have gotten used to seeing.

I considered formalizing the relationship between partials and profile fields (for example, a hash mapping partial names to field names). This idea was discarded because it wouldn't meaningfully simplify the export service, tests, or the partials themselves. A comment containing this information was added instead.

Because of how many fields there are in the `Partner::Profile`, the additions this PR makes are rather verbose and arguably hard to read. I did my best to organize them, but it is a notable tradeoff of this solution.

I considered entirely removing the `Partner.partials_to_show` function and `Partner.ALL_PARTIALS` constant. However, this would require refactoring a number of places that expect the `Partner` model to expose these which seemed outside the scope of this PR. I would recommend this change be made at some point for the sake of code cleanliness.

Currently, the `ExportPartnersCSVService` can only handle being passed a list of partners from one organization. Modifying it to handle partners from more than one organization seemed outside the scope of this PR. 

### Type of change

* New feature
* Documentation update

### How Has This Been Tested?

The export service was manually tested.

The existing `spec/services/exports/export_partners_csv_service_spec.rb` tests were modified to check for the newly added fields.

A test was added to verify that the `ExportPartnersCSVService` respects `partials_to_show`.

Two tests was added to verify that `ExportPartnersCSVService` handles being called with no partials.

The existing `spec/requests/partners_requests_spec.rb` tests were modified to check for the newly added fields.

1.  For table version 6, AbstractHoodieLogRecordScanner ignores the log blocks which belong to inflight instants while scanning. PR fixes the logic so that such log blocks are not ignored. This is required for updating RLI which reads the deleted records from data table
2. hoodie.file.group.reader.enabled needs to be disabled in tbl version 6

6. MarkerBasedRollbackStrategy#createRollbackRequestForCreateAndMerge removes validation that log file should not have IOType as CREATE in table version 6. CREATE is still used for log files with tbl version 6 in LogFileCreationCallback#preFileCreation

pr_title: fix: label generation
pr_body: Resolves #64 ## TL;DR - changed the workflow to fully remove / add labels on issues to regenerate the price and use the proper repo config - stopped running label synchronization on each label addition / removal to save API calls and increase pricing speed - sync happens during an Action run to avoid being killed mid flight - various log improvement and bug fixes ## Changes The workflow updates the labels according to the configuration changes. Instead of forcing an update on all the issues using the updated configuration, now the plugin will remove all the labels from all the issues, update the pricing labels and then add back all the labels except the price. This is because repositories can potentially override the organization configuration thus have different price labels. By updating the set labels, this in turn triggers a run of the plugin that will use the local repository configuration properly. Logs have been improved, and some bugs have been resolved (all the labels were not fetched on update, and I removed the throw when labels were already present which would stop the workflow). ## Workflow To achieve this, I removed the synchronisation of labels for each label added and removed, which seemed quite wrong, using a lot of resources for no reason. Now the synchronisation only happens on issue created, and repository created. This also runs in an Action, so we should have no timeout issue, and the Action can exhaust the retries available if we hit a secondary rate limit. The other benefit is that we get instant pricing updates on the issues as well. The only downside (except if I introduced bugs) is that on issues that do not have labels, we can't use the "good first issue" label add / remove technique to update the labels. This should be okay most of the time since labels get generated on issue creation, but if an issue was created before then it could potentially be a problem (we can always create and delete an empty issue). Eventually if that is needed we could add a command like `/labelRegen` to this plugin, but I don't think that it will be necessary. ## QA For the QA, I used two different repositories in the same organization, one that has a custom configuration and one that using the organization wide configuration. I created, edited and labeled these at the same time. They have different base rate multipliers which is why the price is different. We can see that both were updated properly, despite running updates on the same repository simultaneously. @0x4007 RFC!

pr_title: fix the late-bound customization of the `continues_on` algorithm
pr_body:
## Description

cplusplus/sender-receiver#337 describes a problem with the design of lazy algorithm customization in `std::execution`. i am writing a paper ([D3718](https://isocpp.org/files/papers/D3718R0.html)) that addresses the issue. this PR is an implementation of the "principled approach" described in that paper.

the tl;dr is that, due to an oversight, `connect` uses an incorrect domain tag to find late customizations of the `continues_on` algorithm. this makes execution transfers from, say, a GPU to a CPU rather rather impossible to do at `connect` time. (the GPU scheduler in stdexec uses early customization which is why the problem didn't crop up sooner.)

the solution is to recognize that every sender actually has (at least) two domains:
1. the domain of the execution context on which `start` is called on that sender's operation state, and
2. the domain of the execution context on which `set_value` is called on the receiver used to `connect` the sender.

Early customization should use the `set_value` domain of its predecessor. Late customization uses the `start` domain of the sender being `connect`-ed.

for most senders, the `start` and `set_value` domains are the same. but for `continues_on`, `let_value` and (the non-standard) `sequence` algorithms, they can be different.

this PR breaks the `get_domain` query into `get_domain<start_t>` and `get_domain<set_value_t>`, and it plumbs them through each of the sender algorithms.

pr_title: feat: handle federated logout requests and SAML SLO reponses
pr_body:
# Which Problems Are Solved

Currently if a user signs in using an IdP, once they sign out of Zitadel, the corresponding IdP session is not terminated. This can be the desired behavior. In some cases, e.g. when using a shared computer it results in a potential security risk, since a follower user might be able to sign in as the previous using the still open IdP session.

# How the Problems Are Solved

#9841 already enabled the management of a federated logout option on SAML IdPs. This PR implements it the following way:
- During the termination of a login V1 session using OIDC end_session endpoint, Zitadel will check if an IdP was used to authenticate that session.
- In case there was a SAML IdP used with Federated Logout enabled, it will intercept the logout process, store the information into the shared cache and redirect to the federated logout endpoint in the V1 login.
- The V1 login federated logout endpoint checks every request on an existing cache entry. On success it will create a SAML logout request for the used IdP and either redirect or POST to the configured SLO endpoint. The cache entry is updated with a `redirected` state.
- A SLO endpoint is added to the `/idp` handlers, which will handle the SAML logout responses. At the moment it will check again for an existing federated logout entry (with state `redirected`) in the cache. On success, the user is redirected to the initially provided `post_logout_redirect_uri` from the end_session request.

# Additional Changes

None

# Additional Context

- part of #9228 
- backport to 3.x

+# FluentPermissions Usage Guide
+
+## Introduction
+
+The `FluentPermissions` class is for handling Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) permissions.
+It allows for checking multiple fields against user permissions using a fluent API.
+
+---
+
+## Installation & Setup
+
+Ensure your project includes the necessary imports:
+
+```python
+from metrics.data.models.rbac_models import RBACPermission
+from metrics.api.packages.permissions import FluentPermissions, FluentPermissionsError
+```
+
+---
+
+## Creating FluentPermissions Instance
+
+To create an instance of `FluentPermissions`, pass in the **data** (the object containing the fields to check) 
+and the **group_permissions** (a list of `RBACPermission` objects associated with the user).
+
+### Example:
+```python
+permissions = FluentPermissions(
+    data={
+        "theme": "infectious_disease",
+        "sub_theme": "respiratory",
+        "topic": "COVID-19",
+    },
+    group_permissions=[user_permission_object],
+)
+```
+
+---
+
+## Adding Fields to Check
+
+You must specify which fields you want to check by calling `.add_field(field_name)`. Multiple fields can be chained.
+
+### Example:
+```python
+permissions.add_field("theme").add_field("sub_theme").add_field("topic")
+```
+
+---
+
+## Executing the Permissions Check
+
+Once the fields are added, call `.execute()` to process the matching logic.
+
+### Example:
+```python
+permissions.execute()
+```
+
+The results are stored in `permissions.match_fields_all`, which is a **read-only property** 
+that returns a list of dictionaries indicating whether each field matched.
+
+### Example Output:
+```python
+[
+    {
+        "theme": True,
+        "sub_theme": True,
+        "topic": False,
+        "geography_type": False,
+        "geography": False,
+        "metric": False,
+        "age": False,
+        "stratum": False,
+    }
+]
+```
+
+---
+
+## Validating the Permissions
+
+To ensure that at least one set of permissions fully matches, call `.validate()`.
+If no complete match is found, it raises a `FluentPermissionsError`.
+
+### Example:
+```python
+try:
+    permissions.validate()
+except FluentPermissionsError:
+    print("Access denied")
+```
+---
+
+## Integration with `filter_by_permissions` Decorator
+
+The `FluentPermissions` class is used within the `filter_by_permissions()` decorator to automatically enforce permissions when serializing API responses.
+
+### Example:
+```python
+@filter_by_permissions()
+class MySerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
+    class Meta:
+        model = MyModel
+        fields = "__all__"
+```
+
+When `to_representation()` is called on the serializer, the decorator ensures that unauthorized users cannot see restricted data.
+
+---
+
+## Handling Public Data
+
+If an object contains `is_public = True`, the `FluentPermissions` logic is **bypassed**, and the data is always returned.
+
+### Example:
+```python
+{ "is_public": True, "theme": "Finance", "sub_theme": "Banking" }

pr_title: Inject JS script to restore picture in picture behavior
pr_body:
## Resolves https://github.com/brave/brave-browser/issues/44933

## Releated to https://github.com/brave/brave-core/pull/26355

# 🧐 Reviewer's Notes

1. **The approach is wrong as we should be doing this through a new component, downloading the scripts from a CRX package.**

**Answer:** Implementing the new architecture will require time and multiple PRs. The solution adopted here should be intended as a temporary (and quick) fix to restore the PIP behavior and limit bad user reviews. The solution is also based on the architecture we currently have in production now, so even if is not a state-of-the-art architecture it proved to work correctly and it's battle tested. The solution is based on a minimal set of JS instructions. Instructions that will thoroughly go over a security review to be extra safe.

2. **This solution may stop working again in case of further modification on YouTube website and without the mechanics of a CRX package we cannot propagate a fix in production.**

**Answer:** Correct, this is a possibility we should not exclude. The JS script though was implemented keeping in mind the main priority: zero side effects. In case of breaking changes, the script becomes a no op. On top of that the script will be loaded only when the YouTube background playback option is enabled. Even if suboptimal, this solution can guarantee an extra safety net in case of issues: disabling YouTube background playback option will completely skip the injection offering a pristine version of the YouTube page.

3. **Why the script is not injected in an isolated world ID?**

**Answer:** For similar reasons presented [here](https://github.com/brave/brave-browser/issues/36443), the script needs access to the main YT JS bundle, so main world access is required.

# Description

This PR implements a solution that brings back the PIP behavior.
The PR introduces a very minimal set of JS instructions to inject within a YouTube page.

## Security Review GH issue: https://github.com/brave/reviews/issues/1916

# Update May 6, 2025

Including a small update for posterity in order to recap what has been done and what will be addressed in follow up issues.
This PR implements a strategy to bring back picture in picture support for YouTube videos. Test coverage has been extensively discussed and introduced to make sure:
* We don't have race conditions when injecting the JS script
* We don't inject the script multiple times on same page navigation
* We don't create side effects in case of unexpected changes, and/or serialzed flags don't match
* We inject/modify the serialized flags in case of partial match

After careful considerations we opted to protect the picture in picture feature behind a flag.

The playback video injection has been left as is, and not modified on purpose as we didn't want to mix these two features in this PR. Any improvement and test coverage related to playback video support will be implemented in a follow up PR.

Security & privacy review: ✅ 
Performance review: ✅

## Demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00136119-0a78-4283-ab27-28b110ee85c7

## Test Plan

- Open Brave Browser and navigate to youtube.com
- Search for a random video and play it
- Tap on fullscreen icon within the YT player
- Navigate to the home screen using the swiping gestures or tapping on the home button
- Observe the activity enters picture in picture mode
- Observe the video keeps playing correctly

pr_title: ✨ Add command to update olmv1 operator
pr_body:
Adds command to update an existing olmv1 operator (`ClusterExtension`).

Command has the following signature and flags:
```bash
Update an operator

Usage:
  operator olmv1 update operator <operator> [flags]

Flags:
      --channels stringArray               desired channels for operator versions. AND operation with version. Empty list means all available channels will be taken into consideration
  -h, --help                               help for operator
      --ignore-unset                       when enabled, any unset flag value will not be changed. Disabling means that for each unset value a default will be used instead (default true)
      --labels stringToString              labels that will be set on the operator (default [])
      --selector string                    filters the set of catalogs used in the bundle selection process. Empty means that all catalogs will be used in the bundle selection process
      --upgrade-constraint-policy string   controls whether the upgrade path(s) defined in the catalog are enforced. One of CatalogProvided|SelfCertified), Default: CatalogProvided
      --version string                     desired operator version (single or range) in semVer format. AND operation with channels

pr_title: Add the `aws-load-balancer-controller` to support ServiceType LoadBalancer on EKS
pr_body:
This adds the https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-load-balancer-controller (ALBC) to EKS-based clusters.

With it it's possible to use Services with `Type: LoadBalancer` on EKS with IPv6. It's implemented as an NLB. The controller also takes care of opening and closing the ports on the nodes via updating the security group.

A working service could look like this:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nginx
  annotations:
    # dualstack enables IPv6, there's no IPv6-only option
    # injected: this will be injected by admission-controller on EKS if not defined
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ip-address-type: dualstack
    # configures IPv6 Pod-addresses in the Target Group, bypassing the need to configure nodes (which doesn't work currently)
    # optional: this is the default and can be omitted or changed to `instance`
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-nlb-target-type: ip
    # makes this NLB available via the Internet
    # optional: this is the default and can be omitted or changed to `internal`
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-scheme: internet-facing
    # exposes this port from the below port-list via SSL
    # optional: if not defined, all ports would be used
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-ports: "443"
    # configure a certificate for SSL termination
    # optional: if not defined, no SSL endpoint will be available
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: arn:aws:acm:eu-central-1:1234567890:certificate/some-id
    # configure DNS to point this name to the created NLB
    # optional: if not defined, no custom DNS name will be available. Needed when using SSL.
    external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname: nginx.playground.zalan.do
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  # marks this service for being processed by ALBC rather than the in-tree Service controller
  # injected: this will be injected by admission-controller on EKS if not defined
  loadBalancerClass: service.k8s.aws/nlb
  selector:
    application: nginx
  ports:
    - name: http
      protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80
    - name: https
      protocol: TCP
      port: 443
      targetPort: 80
```

The part that triggers the new controller is:

```yaml
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  loadBalancerClass: service.k8s.aws/nlb
```

which marks the Service as a "load balancer" and gives it a class that's handled by ALBC. This prevents the in-tree, or cloud-provider (formerly in-tree) controllers to process it. `loadBalancerClass` is optional and will be injected by `admission-controller` unless it's already defined.

Another required part is the annotation: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ip-address-type: dualstack`. Since our EKS clusters run on IPv6 this is the only value that works. This annotation is optional and will be injected by `admission-controller` unless it's already defined.

All other annotations are optional but using them either overrides a default or triggers new functionality:
* `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-nlb-target-type: ip`: backend can be registered to load balancers in two modes, IP-mode attaches IPv6 pod IPs, whereas instance-mode attaches instances. Currently, only ip-mode works but it could be changed here.
* `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-scheme: internet-facing`: by default load balancers are internet facing to match the old behaviour. This annotations can be used to make private load balancers.
* `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: arn:aws:acm:eu-central-1:1234567890:certificate/some-id`: optionally enable SSL termination by specifying a certificate. If not set, traffic will be unencrypted.
* `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-ports`: when using SSL, all ports are exposed encrypted. If not desired (such as when doing a typical 80/443 setup) a subset can be selected
* `external-dns.alpha.kubernetes.io/hostname: nginx.playground.zalan.do`: assign a custom DNS name via ExternalDNS. Likely needed when using SSL, otherwise clients will present warnings when the NLB endpoint is used directly.

pr_title: Add mDNS Bridge (mdns-bridge) package
pr_body:
Implements Redmine #15853 (https://redmine.pfsense.org/issues/15853)

mDNS Bridge is intended as an alternative to Avahi reflection for sharing Multicast DNS across network interfaces.

Compared with Avahi, mDNS Bridge is expected to offer several advantages:

- mDNS Bridge is purpose built for bridging mDNS data only.
- Does not retain state across packets (no caching).
- Correctly forwards mDNS NSEC packets.
- Supports newer mDNS packet types such as OPT, SVCB and HTTPS.
- Offers interface specific inbound/outbound filter controls.
- Smaller and simpler code, offering easier inspection/validation.
- Run time memory requirements approximately 1/2 the size of Avahi.

pr_title: HDDS-12596. OM fs snapshot max limit is not enforced
pr_body:
## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

```xml
//ozone-default.xml
<property>
  <name>ozone.om.fs.snapshot.max.limit</name>
  <value>1000</value>
  <tag>OZONE, OM, MANAGEMENT</tag>
  <description>
    The maximum number of filesystem snapshot allowed in an Ozone Manager.
  </description>
</property>
```
The value of the above property is passed to RDBStore but it is never used.

We should verify & limit the number of snapshots created in `OMSnapshotCreateRequest`.

- Get non-deleted rows count directly from `NumSnapshotActive` metrics.
  - It would be prepared on the OM node restart, and be inc/dec on  `TestOMSnapshotCreateRequest`/`TestOMSnapshotDeleteRequest`. So it would reflect the real snapshotTable row count.
https://github.com/apache/ozone/blob/a4d878ef7ad0bd8697fddffa689b8159ca22df1f/hadoop-ozone/ozone-manager/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/ozone/om/OzoneManager.java#L1949-L1980

## What is the link to the Apache JIRA

https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDDS-12596

## How was this patch tested?

CI:
~~https://github.com/peterxcli/ozone/actions/runs/14679627514~~
https://github.com/peterxcli/ozone/actions/runs/14683601913
review_comment:
This approach has an issue. `preExecute` runs only on a single node (the leader node, if I recall correctly), whereas `validateAndUpdateCache` runs on all nodes. If we decrement in `validateAndUpdateCache`, other nodes will keep decrementing without a corresponding increment, causing the value to go negative. Additionally, if leadership changes, it could result in exceeding the allowed limit.

IMO, we can simplify this by relying on the `SnapshotChain` count, which will act as a soft limit initially and eventually become a hard limit. I doubt that `applyingTransaction` is slower than the write request rate to the extent that it would create a backlog of snapshot creation requests.

## What was changed
Introduces `TypedSearchAttributes` to the Typescript SDK, allowing users to supply and receive type-enforced search attributes. `TypedSearchAttributes` are intended to replace the existing (not type-enforced) `SearchAttributes` which have been marked as `@deprecated` in its existing usages.

Brings parity with other SDKs which have a typed search attribute implementation.
Brings parity to how the server represents search attributes.
Provides a typed, structured interface to use search attributes.

pr_title: network: include Chunk Validators in Tier1
pr_body:
Adds chunk validators to the Tier1 participant set. In mainnet, T1 will grow in size from 100 to 250 participants.

Changing the function which calculates the participant set should be sufficient to implement this change. The code in the network crate which initiates outbound connections and accepts incoming ones operates according to the calculated participant set.

-----

OptimisticBlock was being broadcast over Tier1 to all peers. The CVs are not interested in receiving OB, so the behavior is changed to send only to BPs.**

The following message types sent over T1 are not affected in any way:
- `Tier1Handshake`, `HandshakeFailure`, and `LastEdge`, are used only to manage the connection.
- `BlockApproval` is routed specifically to the next block producer.
- `VersionedChunkEndorsement`  is routed specifically to the next few block producers.
- `VersionedPartialEncodedChunk` is routed to the block producers of current and next epochs.
- `ContractCodeRequest` is routed to one randomly chosen chunk producer.
- `ContractCodeResponse` is routed back to the author of the incoming request.

The following routed message types were already allowed on T1 and will now be sent over T1 more consistently:
- `PartialEncodedStateWitness` is routed in parts to all chunk validators.
- `PartialEncodedStateWitnessForward` is routed to all chunk validators.
- `ChunkContractAccesses` is routed to the chunk validators which aren't producers.


**I tested out sending the OB only to the next 5 block producers instead of sending it to all of them, but it caused `tests::optimistic_block::test_optimistic_block` to fail.

pr_title: [query api] don't propagate offset into prefetches
pr_body:
One overlooked quirk when developing prefetches is that we should not propagate the main query offset into them. 

In general terms, offsets are not compatible with prefetches. Let's look at one example:

Imagine we have a vector search prefetch (limit=5), and an order_by main query (limit=3). For simplicity, let's assume letters are point IDs, and numbers are the order_by values
```
with offset 0
prefetch candidates: [a: 5, b: 8, c: 3, d: 9, e: 2]

main query ordering: [e: 2, c: 3, a: 5, b: 8, d: 9]
main query results:  [e: 2, c: 3, a: 5]

----------------------------------------
with offset 3 (propagated)
prefetch candidates: [a: 5, b: 8, c: 3, d: 9, e: 2, f: 6, g: 1, h: 4]

main query ordering: [g: 1, e: 2, c: 3, h: 4, a: 5, f: 6, b: 8, d: 9]
main query results:  [h: 4, a: 5, f: 6] 
```

As you can see, the second query, with an offset is not consistent with the first one. Result `g` will never appear.


With this PR, offset is not propagated anymore, so the limit in the prefetch is the total amount of offsetting that can happen for the request. If the user keeps paginating with offset and a fixed limit, results will be stable, but will eventually lead to an empty result.

pr_title: New subcommand `spack config scopes [-hips]`
pr_body:
List the scopes available in the current environment in descending priority order.

* With `-p|--path-scopes`, list only writable, file-based scopes (ignoring `command_line` and `_builtin`).
* With `-i|--included`, list only included scopes (specified in `include.yaml` or an environment `include:` clause).
* With `-s|--show-paths`, annotate scopes with their directory or file (with non-option argument `section`) locations when appropriate.
* Automatically takes account of `SPACK_DISABLE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true`

Useful for understanding the best scope in which to put a particular specific configuration item, or for debugging "missing" config.

  darwin-sequoia-m1
  $ spack config scopes
  command_line user site system defaults defaults:darwin defaults:base _builtin

pr_title: [Core] Add max files rewrite option for RewriteAction
pr_body:
This is a new option when re-writing data files (Spark Actions) to provide user the ability to limit the number of files re-written to potentially reduce file OPS . This option is named as `max-files-to-rewrite` which takes a positive integer as an input, truncates the file tasks until the value is reached. In case the table has fewer files than the parameter value, all the files are processed for re-write option. A property check to ensure that no value less than 0 has also been put in place to ensure early failure. 

Implementation : 
1. `plan` method in `BinPackRewriteFilePlanner` has been refactored to truncate the list of file scan tasks (and there by files to be processed) 
2. An atomic integer (to ensure consistency in streams) called `fileCountRunner` is used to update counter as the `StructLikeMap<List<List<FileScanTask>>> plan` is processed in parallel
3. In case the size of entire fileScanTask list in a partition is > maxFilesToRewrite +  fileCountRunner, the fileScanTask list is _truncated_ to only add the files until the maxFilesToRewrite value is reached. 
4. `selectedFileGroups` is leveraged to hold the final file groups. 


Testing : 

1. `TestBinPackRewriteFilePlanner::testRewriteMaxFilesOption` is written to handle upper bound use case where the value `max-files-to-rewrite` > total number of files in the table 
2. `TestBinPackRewriteFilePlanner::testRewriteMaxFilesOptionInequality` is written to handle equality use case where the value `max-files-to-rewrite`  > total number of files in the table and the resulting data files after rewrite are less than `max-files-to-rewrite`
3. `textMaxFilesRewriteToOnlyTruncateNeededPartitions` is written to ensure that only needed partitions truncated. 
4. `testInvalidMaxFilesRewriteParam` is written to ensure that all validations (along with error messages) are working as expected
